title: Q4 2025 Pricing Elasticity & Headcount Scenarios
body:
Executive summary:
- Purpose: produce a compact, model-backed view of how pricing moves (elasticity) interact with our Q4 2025 hiring plan and monthly cash burn to converge on a set of actionable hiring/revenue targets for the Executive team. This is an iterative working model; key levers are listed in Assumptions.

Top-line context and target:
- Current trailing ARR (LTM): $42,500,000 (approx).
- Q4 2025 objectives: (1) revenue growth acceleration to reach ~+28% YoY ARR run-rate by end of Q4, (2) maintain gross margin >72% while expanding R&D hiring for Serving Runtime, (3) keep quarterly cash burn under plan with a path to TP 18 months runway post Series C assumptions.

Assumptions (base case):
- Average contract price per unit (hosted API equivalent) = $0.045 / billable unit token-equivalent (internal unit).
- Price points tested: base (1.0x), -10%, -20%, +10% relative to base.
- Price elasticity: initial assumption e = -1.2 (10% price cut => ~12% uplift in volume). We stress test between -0.6 to -2.0.
- Churn: base 3.5% monthly, improved 2.8% with +10% price; worsens to 4.2% at -20% price in downside.
- Headcount ramp: hiring across Eng (serving/runtime), Product, Sales/RevOps, and SRE. Average fully loaded cost by role: IC Eng = $260k/yr, Staff Eng = $420k/yr, Sales AE = $210k/yr, RevOps/CS = $180k/yr. Benefits and taxes = 22% uplift included.
- Hiring timeline: hires begin Aug 1, 2025 and stagger through Dec 2025.

Headcount Plan (summary by org and hire months) - extract of sheet tab:
Columns: Role Type | Count Hires (Q4) | Avg FL Cost/yr | Quarterly incremental cost
- Serving Runtime Eng (IC) | 8 | $260,000 | $520,000 (quarterly assumed ramp factor 0.5 for partial quarter)
- Staff / Senior Eng | 3 | $420,000 | $315,000
- Product PMs | 2 | $200,000 | $100,000
- SRE / Infra | 4 | $240,000 | $240,000
- Sales AEs | 6 | $210,000 | $315,000
- RevOps / CS | 5 | $180,000 | $225,000
- Total Q4 incremental run-rate expense (salary+burden annualized) ~ $2,000,000 impact (note: partial-quarter ramp reduces cash impact in Q4).

Quarterly cash impact detail (model capture):
- Q4 incremental payroll cash (actual payroll paid in Q4) = $1.075M (reflects hire phasing and ramp %).
- One-time hiring/onboarding + recruiting = $220k (estimated).
- Total Q4 incremental people spend = $1.295M.

Pricing Scenarios (revenue and margin implications) - simplified view (all numbers are illustrative and aggregated monthly):
Scenario labels: Downside (-20% price), Moderate downside (-10%), Base, Premium (+10%)
Base inputs: Monthly billable units = 100M units; Price = $0.045 => monthly revenue = $4.5M => quarterly revenue = $13.5M.
- Downside (-20% price): Price = $0.036; elasticity -1.6 => volume uplift = +32% => units = 132M => monthly rev = $4.752M => quarterly = $14.256M (net effect: revenue mildly up vs base even at lower price because elasticity >1).
- Moderate (-10%): Price = $0.0405; elasticity -1.2 => units uplift = +12% => monthly rev = $4.536M => quarterly = $13.608M.
- Premium (+10%): Price = $0.0495; elasticity -0.8 => units drop 8% => monthly rev = $4.554M => quarterly = $13.662M.
Observation: with assumed elasticities, aggressive price cuts do not necessarily reduce revenue; impact on churn and LTV is material and tracked below.

LTV / CAC & churn sensitivity (short-form):
- Base: CAC = $45k per win (avg), gross margin 74% => LTV ~ $230k.
- -20% price: churn increases, LTV decreases to ~ $170k despite higher volume; long-term cohort economics worsen.
- +10% price: LTV increases to ~ $255k but new bookings slow slightly and sales cycle length increases, raising CAC by ~6%.

Sensitivity Matrices (sheet extracts) - decisions to be made by Execs: 
- Matrix A: Hiring tolerance vs revenue outcome. Rows = % revenue delta vs base (-15% .. +15%), Columns = hire reduction steps (0%, -10%, -20% of planned hires). Cells show runway months. Key threshold: if revenue delta <= -8% and hires remain unchanged, runway drops below 12 months.
- Matrix B: Price elasticity vs headcount delta required to hit ARR target. Shows that for elasticity <= -0.9, hitting target requires cutting 8-12 FTE from hiring plan; for elasticity >= -1.4 we can keep hiring plan intact.

Cash runway sensitivity example (quick numbers):
- Base case (no price change, planned hires): runway = 19 months.
- Base + 10% price lift: runway = 22 months (from improved gross margins and higher LTV lowering CAC burn).
- -10% price + worse churn: runway = 15 months.
- -20% price (with elasticity assumed): runway = 13 months but cohort economics deteriorate; long-term risk increases.

Open questions & risks:
1) Elasticity range uncertainty: our current data includes limited price experiments. Need two controlled A/B pricing experiments in Q3 to pin elasticity on core hosted customers (JIRA FIN-342).
2) Cohort LTV measurement: pricing changes can move short-term revenue but materially affect LTV via churn — need a 12-month cohort projection model update (linked Confluence page).
3) Hiring velocity: Recruiting pipeline constraints could delay hires 6-8 weeks and push partial ramp into Q1 2026 — we model both on-time and delayed variants.
4) Competitor actions: if competing price cuts occur, realized elasticity could be higher; conversely, product feature differentiation could lower elasticity.

Recommendations (working):
- Run two targeted pricing A/B tests (1:10k customers; 2-week window) in July-August to refine elasticity prior to final Q4 hiring approvals. (Owner: Jonah Li)
- Approve 60% of the Q4 hiring slate now with gating: (a) if elasticity measured <= -1.0 then freeze non-critical hires and move majority of serving/runtime ramp to early Q1; (b) if elasticity > -1.0 approve full slate.
- Delay non-essential discretionary spend (tools/licenses) of $180k to H1 2026 if downside elasticity observed.

Model notes and assumptions log (important for auditors and FP&A):
- All salary figures are fully-loaded estimates (base + equity accrual + benefits @22%).
- Revenue modeled on billable unit concept correlated to token parity but normalized for customer-contract heterogeneity.
- Cohort churn sensitivity is a first-order estimate; flagged for deeper cohort modeling by Applied ML quant team.

Immediate next steps and owners:
- Jonah Li: run pricing A/B experiment plan and instrumentation (JIRA FIN-342) - due 2025-07-30.
- Maya Patel: finalize revised CAC/LTV cohort workbook and push to Confluence - due 2025-08-12.
- Ava Chen (owner): consolidate final Q4 hiring approval package and present to Exec on 2025-09-22.

Appendix (key sheet snippets copied):
1) Headcount by month (Aug-Sep-Oct-Nov-Dec) with ramp% and hiring status (offer/accepted/onboarding) - live columns in the sheet.
2) Per-role comp curves and comp band medians.
3) Scenario outputs table (detailed): rows = [Base, -10%, -20%, +10%] and columns = [Quarterly rev, Quarterly gross margin, Q4 incremental payroll cash, Q4 one-time hiring cost, Runway months].

Notes to reviewers: this is a working model and intentionally slightly conservative on CAC estimates. Please comment inline on the sheet tab 'Assumptions' where you see alternative priors.

Document history: initial draft 2025-06-05 (Ava Chen), updates after recruitment survey 2025-07-18 (Maya), added elasticity runs 2025-08-21 (Jonah), prepared for Exec 2025-09-14 (Ava).
